L01.why: NAMED MECHANISM: geometric run 10/20/40 with 20 as the middle term; 8 is the off-grid stray. Run-middle channel.

L02.why: NAMED MECHANISM: same 10/20/40 run as L01, middle term 20. 6.67 (=20/3) is the only non-integer and reads as a divide-instead-of-multiply slip, not a key.

L03.why: guess — 36/-36 is a sign-flip pair so the key is probably one of them, but nothing blind separates them. 36+54=90 is the round-constant channel, which measured as NOISE, so I did not use it.

L04.why: NAMED MECHANISM: arithmetic run 5/9/13 (d=4), key is the middle term; 6 is the stray.

L05.why: NAMED MECHANISM: arithmetic run 2/3/4 (d=1), middle term 3; 11 is the magnitude outlier and in SAT maths the outlier is a unit/slip distractor.

L06.why: guess — 4/-4 sign-flip pair plus 2 and -3 unpaired; picked the positive member of the flip pair on the weak prior that sign-error distractors mirror the key.

L07.why: guess — complete 2x2 sign x coefficient grid (+/- crossed with 1/x vs 1/(3x)). Perfectly balanced by construction; no option is distinguishable. Flat 25%.

L08.why: guess — 3, 2.25, 0.4, 1.8 share no run or ratio structure I can trust. 2.25 (=9/4) reads as the most computed-looking value, which is a taste judgement, not a mechanism.

L09.why: NAMED MECHANISM: literal-equation 2x2 grid (sign +/- crossed with grouping (xz+/-1)/3 vs xz/3+/-1). In rearrangement items the key is normally the fully-grouped form, and the ungrouped pair are order-of-operations distractors. Picked grouped + minus; the sign is still a coin flip.

L10.why: NAMED MECHANISM: 28 = 4 x 7 is the product-of-two-options distractor (multiplied where one should divide), and -4 is the sign-flip of 4. Eliminating the product leaves 4 as the anchored member of the flip pair.

L11.why: guess — 2.5 is the only non-integer and 0 and -6 are both present, which usually means a quadratic with a discarded root. The only-non-integer channel measured as NOISE here, so this is little better than a lean.

L12.why: guess — 18 = 3 x 6 is a product pair, so 18 is more likely a distractor; 27 = 3^3 is the cube-shaped value in a set that looks exponential. Weak.

L13.why: guess — 14 = 5 + 9 fires the sum-of-two channel, but that channel measured BELOW its null (obs 3 vs exp 4.3), so I refused to use it and took 9 instead on no real evidence.

L14.why: guess — all four negative; -25 is the only perfect-square-derived value, which fits a completing-the-square minimum. Taste, not a mechanism; it is also the smallest option, which the magnitude channel warns against.

L15.why: guess — 11 and 12 are an off-by-one pair so the key is probably one of them; nothing separates them blind.

L16.why: guess — 18 is the magnitude outlier and outliers in this bank read as slips; that leaves 5, -7, -3 with no structure between them.

L17.why: NAMED MECHANISM: arithmetic run 800/1200/1600, key is the middle term; 20 is an order-of-magnitude outlier (80x) and reads as a rate-vs-total unit error. Note the competing read: 800 doubling to 1600 would make 1600 the key, so the run-middle call is contested.

L18.why: NAMED MECHANISM: arithmetic run 0.5/1.5/2.5 (d=1), middle term 1.5; -4 is the only negative and the only integer, doubly off-texture.

L19.why: guess — -16 is the only perfect-square-derived value in a set containing 0, fitting a vertex-minimum item. -16 + 9 = -7 is a sum-channel hit that I discarded as NOISE.

L20.why: NAMED MECHANISM: 2x2 grid, coefficient {2,8} crossed with y^3 numerator/denominator. 8 = 2^3, so the coefficient-cubed forms are correct and the 2 forms are the classic forgot-to-cube-the-coefficient distractors. That halves the field; numerator vs denominator is then a coin flip.

L21.why: guess — two doubling pairs (10/20 and 12/24) with no third term to break the symmetry.

L22.why: NAMED MECHANISM: three options share the 2x^2 frame with constants 1/3, 3, 9 forming a geometric run whose middle is 3; 18x^2+19 is the lone structural outlier (different leading coefficient) and reads as a substitute-wrong-way distractor.

L23.why: NAMED MECHANISM: geometric run 9/18/36 (r=2), key is the middle term; 29 is off-grid.

L24.why: guess — 100 = 10^2 is an order-of-magnitude outlier and 11 = 10+1 is an off-by-one of 10, so 10 is the value both distractors are derived FROM, which usually means the key. Weakly mechanical at best.
